question: How much is a customer liable for if an unauthorised electronic banking transaction is reported on the 5th working day?
retrieved (file p.page): RBI (Customer Protection) Direction.pdf p.5 | RBI (Customer Protection) Direction.pdf p.3 | RBI (Customer Protection) Direction.pdf p.3 | Chapter I Preliminary.pdf p.57 | Chapter I Preliminary (2).pdf p.11
bot_answer: A customer is liable for the transaction value or the amount mentioned in Table 1, whichever is lower, if the unauthorised transaction is reported on the 5th working day [2]. This applies when the responsibility for the unauthorised transaction lies neither with the bank nor with the customer, but elsewhere in the system [3].
expected_answer: Within 4 to 7 working days: the transaction value or the amount in Table 1, whichever is lower. (Within 3 working days = zero liability; beyond 7 days = as per the bank's Board approved policy.)

question: Within how many working days must a bank credit back (shadow reversal) the amount of an unauthorised electronic transaction?
retrieved (file p.page): RBI (Customer Protection) Direction.pdf p.5 | RBI (Customer Protection) Direction.pdf p.5 | RBI (Customer Protection) Direction.pdf p.2 | RBI (Master Circular 2025) Direction.pdf p.3 | RB-IOS, 2026.pdf p.8
bot_answer: A bank must credit back (shadow reversal) the amount of an unauthorised electronic transaction within 10 working days from the date of such notification by the customer [2].
expected_answer: Within 10 working days from the date the customer notifies the bank.

question: What is the maximum exposure of an urban co-operative bank to a single borrower and to a group of connected borrowers?
retrieved (file p.page): RBI (Master Circular 2025) Direction.pdf p.3 | RBI (Master Circular 2025) Direction.pdf p.5 | RBI (Master Circular 2025) Direction.pdf p.8 | Chapter II Financial Institutions Soundness and Resilience.pdf p.14 | Chapter II Financial Institutions Soundness and Resilience.pdf p.14
bot_answer: The maximum exposure of an urban co-operative bank (UCB) to a single borrower is 15 per cent of Tier-I capital, and to a group of connected borrowers is 25 per cent of Tier-I capital [2].
expected_answer: Individual borrower: 15 per cent of Tier-I capital; group of connected borrowers/parties: 25 per cent of Tier-I capital.

question: Can a bank offer NRE or NRO term deposits without a premature withdrawal option?
retrieved (file p.page): RBI DBR 2015-16 19.pdf p.12 | RBI DBR 2015-16 19.pdf p.12 | RBI DBR 2015-16 19.pdf p.8 | Chapter I Preliminary (2).pdf p.44 | Chapter I Preliminary (2).pdf p.15
bot_answer: Yes, a bank can offer NRE or NRO term deposits without a premature withdrawal option, provided that all NRE / NRO term deposits accepted from individuals (held singly or jointly) for an amount of Rupees one crore and below shall have the premature-withdrawal-facility [1].
expected_answer: Yes, but NRE / NRO term deposits from individuals (singly or jointly) of Rs one crore and below must have the premature withdrawal facility.

question: Until when can a bank keep allowing all transactions for a low-risk individual customer whose KYC update is overdue?
expected_file: Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer (KYC)) (Amendment).pdf
retrieved (file p.page): Chapter I Preliminary.pdf p.41 | Chapter I Preliminary.pdf p.41 | Chapter I Preliminary.pdf p.63 | RBI (FAQ3) Direction.pdf p.1 | Forthcoming Instructions.pdf p.2
bot_answer: A bank can keep allowing all transactions for a low-risk individual customer whose KYC update is overdue until June 30, 2026, whichever is later [2].
expected_answer: The RE must allow all transactions and get the KYC updated within one year of it falling due or up to June 30, 2026, whichever is later, and monitor such accounts regularly.

question: How many reminders must a regulated entity send a customer before the due date for periodic KYC updation?
